claims.text: Spin-polarized DFT with a non-collinear spin treatment can reveal a ferromagnetic ground state in transition-metal compounds.
Spin-polarized non-collinear DFT properly captures exchange and correlation effects and the actual spin alignment.
Standard non-spin-polarized approaches do not properly capture the exchange, correlation, and spin-alignment effects needed to identify ferromagnetic ground states.
Explicitly including non-collinear spin degrees of freedom changes the resolved magnetic ordering and local spin arrangements.
Calculations that neglect spin polarization fail to resolve energy differences between magnetic configurations.
Allowing non-collinear spin orientations captures subtle exchange interactions that favor ferromagnetic alignment.
The ferromagnetic state is expected to have lower total energy than antiferromagnetic or non-magnetic states.
Detectable local magnetic moments would confirm ferromagnetic ordering.
Non-spin-polarized DFT often produces an incorrect magnetic-state prediction because it omits spin degrees of freedom.
The approach is applicable when the primary magnetic interactions are adequately described by DFT.
Exceptionally strong electron correlations can limit the approach.
Dominant spin-orbit interactions can limit the approach.
Calculated energy differences and local magnetic moments depend on the exchange-correlation functional and computational parameters.

contradictions.description: The mechanism and baseline say that failure of non-spin-polarized DFT to produce magnetic moments demonstrates its inadequacy, whereas the falsification rule says that such a failure would falsify the claimed advantage of spin-polarized non-collinear DFT. That result would instead tend to support the stated rationale.
